RagShortTexts: In 1241 at Mohi, Batu and Subutai outflanked King Béla IV across the Sajó River,.

Variants.Content: Batu Khan and Subutai attacked King Béla IV along the Sajó River at Mohi on April 11, 1241. The Hungarians had drawn their wagons into a laager on the plain, and Mongol catapults worked to contest the bridge over the river. Subutai's men crossed the marshes downstream and threatened the rear of the Hungarian position. Caught inside the wagon ring, the Hungarian army was routed, and Béla fled. The battle opened the way for the Mongols to ravage the Hungarian plain and strike deep into central Europe. It also showed how a kingdom's field army could be destroyed in a single afternoon, which pushed the crown toward a new defensive strategy built on stone.

The Mongol devastation at Mohi drove Béla IV to rebuild the kingdom's defences. Lords across Hungary were ordered to raise stone castles on their lands, which cost the peasant labour that carried the stone and built the walls. Lords who could not pay the cost lost their claims to the new fortresses.
